questions.q: What did Xenophanes argue about the Greek gods?
a: They were mortal heroes later given divine stories
They were invented by poets for money
They were aliens who visited Greece
They were kings who ruled for centuries
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Xenophanes saw the gods as great humans whose deeds grew into grand origin myths over time.

questions.q: What was Martin Luther trying to do when he challenged the Catholic Church?
a: Refine the church rather than destroy it
Replace the Bible with his own writings
Found a completely new religion
Gain political power over the church
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Luther wanted to correct teachings he found inconsistent with the Bible, which led to Protestantism.

questions.q: What did the Greek philosopher Thales achieve by questioning traditional explanations?
a: He predicted a solar eclipse
He mapped the known world
He measured the height of pyramids
He discovered the atom
questions.why: Lesson 2 credits Thales, the first Western philosopher, with accurately predicting an eclipse in 585 BCE.

questions.q: What did Descartes conclude from his inability to dismiss his doubts?
a: The doubts proved that he existed
The senses are the only reliable guide
God must exist by definition
Nothing at all can be known
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Descartes reasoned that if he were not real, he could not be doubting everything.

questions.q: How does doubt help us deal with death, according to the summary?
a: It shows that worrying about it is pointless
It proves that an afterlife exists
It makes us fear death less over time
It encourages us to postpone thinking about it
questions.why: Lesson 3 says since death is inevitable and unknowable, doubt helps us stop worrying and meet it calmly.
